To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have generated two hiPSC cell lines from the same PCD patient carrying the same mutation.
we have generated and characterized two human induced pluripotent stem cell lines derived from a PCD homozygous mutation carrier.
we generated two hiPSC cell lines from a PCD patients carrying a mutation in the CCNO gene and that these lines are characterized in detail.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of hiPSC lines for the investigation of PCD pathogenesis.

the generation of two human induced pluripotent stem cell lines (hiPSCs) from a primary cilium dyskinesia type 13 (PCD13) patient carrying a homo-zygous duplication in exon 1 (c.248_252dupGATGC) of the cyclin O (CCN) gene (NM_024312.2).
the generation of hiPSCs from a PCD-patient carrying a homozyggotic 5 bp insertion in exon 1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these hiPSC lines are suitable for the investigation of PCD pathophysiological aspects.
this work describes the generation, characterization and differentiation of two hiPSc lines from a patient carrying a mutation of the CCNO-gene.
the hiPSC lines MHHi016-A and MHHi016-B are a valuable resource for studying PCD and the underlying CCNO gene function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully generated hiPSC from a PCD donor carrying the mutation c. 248_250dup (p.Glu84Cysfs*9) in exon 1 in CCNO gene.
we successfully established two hiPSC cell lines (MHHi16-A and MHHi16-B) from a PCD affected patient.
we have generated hiPSC lines from PCD patients and we have characterized the lines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hiPSCs from PCD patients can be used as a model to study the role of CCNO in ciliogenesis and to investigate the effects of CCNO mutations on cell cycle and proliferation.
hiPSCs from a patient with a CCNO mutation are suitable to study the pathogenic mechanisms associated with this mutation and to test potential therapies.
CCNO is involved in the regulation of cilia number and length, as well as in cell proliferation, and that these effects are not restricted to respiratory tract cells.
